name: Linsley et al. NeurIPS 2021 - tracking without re-recognition among identical distractors (PathTracker, InT)
bibliography: Drew Linsley, Girik Malik, Junkyung Kim, Lakshmi N. Govindarajan, Ennio Mingolla, Thomas Serre. Tracking Without Re-recognition in Humans and Machines. NeurIPS 2021 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34) [uncertain - venue taken from the outline and memory; the arXiv listing itself names no venue]; preprint arXiv:2105.13351 (v1 27 May 2021, v2 3 Jun 2021) - same study. Code, PathTracker data and psychophysics: http://bit.ly/InTcircuit (as stated in the paper; repository contents not inspected).
full_text_checked: Short screening: arXiv abstract page and the ar5iv HTML full text (PathTracker setup, Fig. 3-6, Table 1, appendix references to Table S1, Fig. S3/S4 ablations). The PDF itself exceeded the fetch size limit; supplementary figures and code were not opened directly, ablation magnitudes from Fig. 5e/S3/S4 were read only as text descriptions.
task_and_output: PathTracker: binary decision whether the target dot, cued in the first frame, ends at a marked goal location after moving among identical-looking distractor dots (output: one yes/no logit per video). Natural video: InT added to TransT single-object tracker, output is the TransT box.
data_and_independent_videos: PathTracker synthetic: 20K training videos (32 frames, 14 distractors); test variants with 1/14/25 distractors and 32/64/128 frames; human study with about 180 recruited (appendix says 120; filtering inconsistently reported) plus 90 in a second experiment. Natural video: TransT training data; evaluation on standard unseen test sets TrackingNet, LaSOT, GOT-10k plus synthetic perturbations of GOT-10k (colour inversion, random colour inversion, random occlusion).
target_size_and_input_resolution: PathTracker frames 32x32x3 (humans shown 256x256); dots occupy a few pixels [uncertain - dot size not stated]. Natural video: TransT search region (256x256 in TransT, not restated) [uncertain].
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: PathTracker: 10 fps rendering for humans (4, 8, 14 s), static background, no camera motion; objects move on smooth random paths and cross. Natural video: benchmark frame rates, unmodelled camera motion.
detector_and_exemplar: No detector. PathTracker: target marked by a colour cue in the first frame only; afterwards all dots are identical (no appearance exemplar usable). TransT: first-frame box template.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: InT (Index-and-Track) circuit: a recurrent convolutional circuit with excitatory and inhibitory units, divisive/subtractive inhibition and multiplicative/additive excitation, softplus rectification and a learned attention map that gates recurrent activity; all weights trained end-to-end with binary cross-entropy on the final decision (Adam). InT+TransT: InT inserted into TransT and trained with the TransT tracking losses [uncertain - integration details not read].
controls_seeds_splits: Controls: 3D CNNs (R3D and variants), optic-flow R3D, TimeSformer (ImageNet-pretrained and scratch), Conv-GRU, lesioned InT variants (no divisive/subtractive, no multiplicative/additive, no attention, tanh instead of softplus, spatial-softmax attention). Tests on harder generalisation sets (more distractors, longer videos). Seeds and intervals for PathTracker accuracies not reported in the text read [uncertain]; natural-video results are single runs.
metrics_and_numbers: PathTracker (Fig. 3): InT is the only model inside the human confidence interval on all versions; CNNs and pretrained TimeSformer reach the human interval only at 32 frames/14 distractors; no CNN/transformer at 32 frames/25 distractors; Conv-GRU at chance. Fig. 5: InT decisions correlate with human decisions (Pearson rho, Cohen kappa). Ablations (Fig. 5e, S3, S4): every lesion degrades on harder sets; spatial-softmax (single-object) attention worse than CNNs. Table 1 (AUC / Pnorm / P): TrackingNet TransT 81.4 / 86.7 / 80.3 vs InT+TransT 81.94 / 87.48 / 80.94; LaSOT 64.9 / 73.8 / 69.0 vs 65.0 / 74.0 / 69.3; GOT-10k AO 72.3 vs 72.2. GOT-10k perturbations (AO): colour inversion 40.7 vs 43.1, random colour inversion 57.5 vs 62.5, random occlusion 55.2 vs 56.9. No intervals.
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (new synthetic videos; standard test sets). Target absence: no (PathTracker target always present; refusal not modelled). Similar distractors: yes - identical distractors are the core of PathTracker; in natural video not separately measured. Occlusion: synthetic random occlusion on GOT-10k only; in PathTracker only crossings. Night/low light: no (colour inversion is the closest perturbation). Sequential operation on own predictions: yes within the recurrent circuit (online state); no re-detection.
mechanism_summary: Published: a recurrent excitatory/inhibitory circuit keeps an attention 'index' on the cued object and moves it frame by frame using local motion continuity, not appearance; inhibition suppresses competitors and the attention can split across objects at crossings (implicit multi-object tracking). Tracking succeeds only if every intermediate frame is seen at a rate where displacement stays within the circuit's local neighbourhood. Proposed modification for us (not published): use FlyVis motion-type activity as the input of a small recurrent attention/index state that is propagated across frames during track loss, instead of re-recognising the target from an exemplar.
transfer_limits: (1) Density: PathTracker needs every frame with small displacements; our labels are 5 fps and the crop moves and rescales, so a target displacement between processed frames can exceed the local neighbourhood of an index map on 721 hexals; at 30 Hz with crop ego-motion compensation the displacement per frame is plausible but the crop shift itself must be subtracted. (2) Index must start on the target: InT needs a correct cue at onset and continuous observation; our task begins after the track is lost (target possibly occluded or missed by the detector for many frames), exactly the regime where motion-only indexing has nothing to carry. (3) Synthetic dots on static background; BDD100K has camera motion, scale change and clutter. (4) Natural-video gain is tiny on clean benchmarks (+0.5 AUC TrackingNet, +0.1 LaSOT, -0.1 GOT-10k) and appears mainly under appearance perturbations, which are not our failure (our failure is similar neighbours with similar motion). (5) Targets ~9x12 lattice steps are large compared with PathTracker dots; crossings of vehicles produce merged motion blobs. (6) No refusal output. (7) YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA already provide motion continuity via Kalman; an index state duplicating it may add nothing.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1: caution - shows that continuity of a motion index can disambiguate identical objects without re-recognition, but only while the target is continuously visible; gives no refusal mechanism. 5.2: design analogy - a propagated recurrent state as 'memory' of where the target is, alternative to appearance memory. 5.3: indirect - InT is trained end-to-end on the applied decision (BCE on final answer), an example of a loss on the applied decision rather than an intermediate map. 5.4: not addressed (single-object; no association).
candidate_node_change: Node: state/readout - a recurrent 'index' map over the 721 hexals, driven by FlyVis T4/T5-type motion outputs, carried across frames while the track is visible and continued for a few frames into loss; the predicted centre is the index peak. Control without FlyVis: the same recurrent index driven by frame differences / optical flow of the grey crop (eye input) and the ByteTrack Kalman prediction alone. Control with stock FlyVis: same index on stock FlyVis outputs (ensemble 000). Minimal check: on train26 loss episodes, fraction of episodes where the index after k=1..5 frames of loss stays within the gate of the true box versus Kalman; requires 30 Hz frames, not 5 fps labels. Stop condition: if index accuracy after 3 frames of loss is not better than Kalman by a pre-registered margin with a bootstrap interval excluding zero, stop; do not proceed to HOTA. Assessment: low priority - it addresses short crossings, not re-finding after longer loss, which is the Z13 failure.
strongest_objection: The mechanism explicitly avoids re-recognition and therefore cannot re-acquire a target after it was lost or occluded beyond the circuit's carry-over; Z13 is precisely re-finding after loss among similar neighbours. Its natural-video benefit is within noise on clean benchmarks and is appearance-perturbation robustness, not distractor discrimination.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (NeurIPS 2021) [uncertain venue verification], code announced; no independent replication found in this screening. Strength: moderate for the synthetic claim (human-matched, ablations), weak for natural-video transfer (single runs, <=0.5 AUC differences without intervals).
where_distinction_is_made: In the recurrent dynamics (representation/state): the attention index is maintained by excitation following motion continuity and inhibition of competitors; there is no explicit target model, no memory of appearance, no separate decision for 'target outside area' or 'insufficient data'. A map maximum is equated with the target by construction (the index is the target as long as continuity holds); presence of the right object is never tested.
feature_dependence: PathTracker shows the circuit works with no appearance information at all (identical dots, 32x32 input), i.e. small motion features suffice for the synthetic task. In natural video it is bolted onto TransT, whose appearance features carry the tracking; the circuit's motion route only adds robustness under appearance perturbation. So: evidence for small motion features exists only on synthetic dots with static background.
association_consequence: Not linked to detection association (single-object). For us an index centre would enter as a prediction centre during loss; the same effect for short gaps is largely given by the ByteTrack Kalman prediction, and the R1 case shows that a wrong centre correction can raise the correct match cost (0.123 -> 1.0). An external guard (shift limit relative to Kalman, cost check) would give the safe part of the effect without the mechanism.
difference_from_tried: Different from everything tried in Z13: no exemplar matching, no target model, no memory of observations - instead continuous motion-based state propagation from the last visible frame (no re-recognition). The project did not try a recurrent index carried through loss. However, the project's earlier finding that FlyVis does not beat its input under the same readout, and Kalman already providing continuity, mean the difference may not translate into benefit.
memory_write_policy: Not applicable (no explicit memory; only recurrent state updated every frame).
distractor_representation: Implicit: competitors are suppressed through learned inhibition in the recurrent circuit; no buffer or negative class.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Not applicable - no refusal; final decision accumulates over the whole video but only for the yes/no goal question.
loss_on_applied_decision: Yes for PathTracker (BCE on the final yes/no answer actually reported); for InT+TransT the TransT tracking loss on box/classification [uncertain].
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the source; if transferred - state update / prediction centre before matching.
no_fly_control_equivalent: ByteTrack Kalman constant-velocity prediction; optical-flow propagation of the last box (e.g. Lucas-Kanade on the grey crop); the same recurrent index driven by frame differences of the eye input.
hard_subset_evaluation: PathTracker difficulty levels (25 distractors, 64/128 frames) and GOT-10k perturbation subsets (synthetic, chosen by the authors); no natural hard-distractor subset.
temporal_information_availability: Causal: the recurrent state uses only current and past frames; the PathTracker decision is read at the last frame (offline yes/no), but per-frame index is available online with no latency beyond one frame. Requires dense frames; with our 5 fps labels the state must run on the 30 Hz stream.
depth_level: Short screening. Lost: the mechanism tracks through continuity and cannot re-find a lost target; natural-video gains are small and concern appearance perturbations, not similar distractors; no refusal. Should not move to full analysis; keep as explanation that motion continuity alone is not the Z13 answer.
